text:
Ashley (oncall): Seeing huge GPU churn in us-west1 — autoscaler spun up ~40 g5 nodes in <10m and we're now hitting project quota alerts. dashboards show batch-inference namespace responsible. :alarm_clock:

devops-bot: [alert] cluster-autoscaler: rapid_scale_up detected on cluster: redwood-prod-us-west1 (severity: high)

raj: :eyes: I see a bunch of pods in CrashLoopBackOff and some long-running batch jobs with no resource limits. Can you paste `kubectl top nodes`?

Ashley (oncall): Pasted quick outputs: ```
NAME                 CPU(cores)   CPU%   GPU(alloc)
node-g5-1            120m         6%     1/1
node-g5-2            110m         5%     1/1
... many nodes added quickly (40 total) ...
```

sylvie: How are auto-scale settings? Maybe scale-up threshold is too aggressive or expander is set to least-waste. Also check cloud provider quota for GPUs — if we hit quota, new pods queue and CA may spin more requests.

noah: I just looked at the autoscaler configmap: `--scale-up-delay=0s`, `--max-node-provision-time=15m`, and max nodes for node-pool-burst is 60. That's why it exploded.

raj: Immediate mitigations: 1) cordon the burst pool so CA can't create more there, 2) patch problematic batch jobs to suspend/start with smaller replicas, 3) apply a namespace ResourceQuota to cap GPU requests to stop further spin-ups.

Ashley (oncall): Doing 1 now: ```
kubectl cordon node-pool-g5-burst-xyz
kubectl taint nodes -l pool=burst gpu-burst=true:NoSchedule
```

kevin: Heads up — finance: that's already ~$23k projected for the hour if this keeps going. If we can switch newly-provisioned nodes to preemptible instead of on-demand we can save, but right now we should prioritize containment.

infra-sre: I've started patching the HPA for batch-runner to hard cap replicas to 3: ```
kubectl patch hpa batch-runner -n batch-inference -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":3}}'
```

noah: Also evict the runaway pods to force them to restart on tainted nodes or be rescheduled under quota: ```
kubectl get pods -n batch-inference -o name | grep run-job | xargs -n1 kubectl delete -n batch-inference --grace-period=0 --force
```

ops-bot: notice: cloudquota-alert: GPU quota at 96% in project redwood-prod-us-west1. Requesting emergency quota increase requires 45+ min.

sylvie: Since quota increase is slow, we should: A) scale down CA aggressiveness (scale-up-delay=30s, max-node-provision-time=10m), B) set cluster-autoscaler expander to priority and prefer existing pools, C) add scaleDownUnneededTime to 10m so we don't thrash. I'll push a config change to the CA configmap.

raj: Can one of you run the CA config patch? I don't want to do it during the spike.

noah: I'll apply now: ```
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap cluster-autoscaler-status --patch '{"data":{"scale-up-delay":"30s","max-node-provision-time":"10m","scaleDownUnneededTime":"10m","expander":"least-waste"}}'
```

Ashley (oncall): After those mitigations, node creation rate dropped. We still have many active nodes but pod backlog is clearing. Monitoring CPU/GPU utilization and the job queue. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Please open a cost incident ticket and flag affected namespaces for chargeback. We'll reconcile.

infra-sre: Postmortem action items suggested now: 1) Namespace-level GPU quota defaults for batch/adhoc, 2) HPA safe defaults for known batch controllers, 3) CA config guardrails (max-burst-per-pool, min-scale-up-delay), 4) implement per-namespace priority classes so preemptible jobs don't block prod.

sylvie: Also add a short circuit in our provisioning flow: if project GPU quota >90% then fallback to throttling new create requests for non-critical namespaces.

Ashley (oncall): Summary: cordoned burst pool, capped HPAs, evicted runaway pods, patched CA to reduce aggressiveness. Back to monitoring; filing postmortem. Thanks team. :pray:

ops-bot: incident:update: status=mitigated, severity=high, incident_id=INC-2025-0432

kevin: Add follow-up: schedule a runbook refresh and an automated test that simulates a scaling storm against staging CA.

raj: I'll own the runbook and CA guardrails ticket. Assigning to infra-sre for implementation.

Ashley (oncall): Last check — CPU/GPU utilization stabilizing and no new node launches for 7m. Closing this thread but keeping dashboards open for 1h.
